$comment: This model also enforces floor <= total_floors (see _floor_within_building below), but that invariant is NOT reflected anywhere else in this schema. Unlike Availability's mode/on_date invariant above, this one compares two sibling fields' VALUES to each other, not a field to a literal constant -- expressing that in standard JSON Schema would need a $data-style same-document reference, which draft 2020-12 (the draft this schema targets) does not include in its core spec. A consumer validating records in another language must re-implement this specific check itself; this comment exists so that requirement is visible in the schema artifact itself, not only in this file's Python source.

neighborhood.description: Optional: Facebook Marketplace and some Yad2 posts give only a street or a city, no named neighborhood. Required-by-default here would reject real, otherwise-usable listings. A fourth external review caught that 'optional' had been implemented as 'Optional[str]', not 'optional NonEmptyStr' -- so None correctly meant 'not known', but '' or ' ' also validated, silently meaning the same thing as None through a second, unintended spelling. That second spelling is what breaks dedup: street='' and street=None are the same real-world fact ('we don't have one') but are NOT the same string, so exact-match comparison treats them as different addresses.
neighborhood.title: Neighborhood

on_date.description: Required when mode == DATE, forbidden otherwise (enforced below, and reflected in the exported JSON Schema via an if/then/else block -- see _availability_json_schema_extra) -- without that invariant, mode=DATE with on_date=None is a state that claims a specific date exists without saying what it is. Named on_date rather than `date` to avoid shadowing the `date` type within this class's own annotations.
on_date.title: On Date

phone.description: Normalized to E.164 on input (e.g. both '054-123-4567' and '+972 54 123 4567' become '+972541234567') -- this is the primary anchor for cross-platform deduplication, so two representations of the same number must produce the exact same string, not just similar-looking ones. Currently assumes an Israeli local number when no country code is present (leading '0' -> '+972'), since that's the only market this tool operates in today; a non-Israeli number with no '+' is ambiguous and is returned digits-only rather than guessed. A third external review caught that this used to skip length validation entirely, so a truncated/mistyped number like '054-123' silently produced a plausible-looking but invalid '+97254123' -- it now requires exactly 9 digits after the trunk '0' for a mobile number (05X-XXXXXXX) or 8 for a landline (0X-XXXXXXX), falling back to the 'ambiguous, don't guess' branch otherwise, same as a number with no leading 0.
phone.title: Phone

url.description: A real URI, not just any string -- a third external review caught that a plain `str` here both accepts garbage (empty string, a bare filename) and exports as an untyped JSON Schema string with no `format: "uri"` for another language's validator to check against. `AnyUrl` fixes both.
url.title: Url

ListedBy.description:
Whether the listing comes from the owner directly or an agency.

Usually a structured fact the source platform states outright (Yad2
marks this explicitly); where it's only inferable from free text,
treat it as a `Signal` under `signals["listed_by"]` instead of forcing
it in here -- this field is for the cases we're confident about.

Deliberately NOT extended with SUBLET / LEASE_TRANSFER members, even
though a fourth external review correctly pointed out that a sublet
(סאבלט) or a lease transfer (מחליף/ה) fits neither PRIVATE nor
AGENCY cleanly. The review's diagnosis was right; its implied fix
(add more values to this enum) would have been wrong, because
"who is listing it" (private person vs. agency) and "what kind of
tenancy is being offered" (a fresh lease vs. a sublet vs. a lease
transfer) are two independent facts, not one -- a sublet is
typically posted by a private individual, so it's PRIVATE *and* a
sublet, not a third option that can't also be private. Collapsing
them into one field would make it impossible to represent that
combination at all. The right place for "is this a sublet" is
`signals["sublet"]` (or `signals["lease_transfer"]`) -- which needs
NO schema change, because `signals` was already designed in Phase 0
to be an open map for exactly this kind of free-text-derived fact.
No detection rule is added for it yet, on the same "verify against
real data before writing a rule" standard as everything else in
migrate.py: the live 22-listing dataset has no sublet or
lease-transfer example to check a rule against.
ListedBy.title: ListedBy

RecurringCosts.description:
Secondary monthly costs on top of base rent. Omitted entirely
(left as None on Listing) rather than zero-filled when unknown --
zero would wrongly assert "no arnona," which is never true in
practice and would distort a true-monthly-cost calculation.
RecurringCosts.title: RecurringCosts

Signal.description:
A tagged union representing one fact extracted from a listing's free
text (balcony mention, roommate-exclusion language, bike storage, ...).

`status` is the tag. `value` is only meaningful when status is
CONFIRMED or CONTRADICTED; it is intentionally optional so "we don't
know yet" (UNKNOWN) and "we looked and it's ambiguous" (UNCONFIRMED)
are representable without inventing a fake value.

evidence.description: Short quote or excerpt supporting this signal's status.
evidence.title: Evidence

Signal.title: Signal

SignalStatus.description: Confidence state for a fact extracted from free text.
SignalStatus.title: SignalStatus

description:
The canonical record for one rental listing, from any source, in
any city. Nothing in this model may refer to a specific user's
preferences (no `balcony: bool` field, for instance) -- preference
facts live in `signals`, keyed by whatever preference a given user
cares about.

id.description: Stable id for THIS SOURCE POST, e.g. hash of source + source_listing_id. Deliberately distinct from apartment_id below -- this id must stay stable and unique per post even before any cross-platform matching has run.
id.title: Id

apartment_id.description: Cross-platform entity id for the physical apartment this post describes. Null until a deduplication step (Phase 2/3) resolves two posts -- e.g. the same unit cross-posted to Yad2 and Facebook -- to the same apartment_id, typically by matching normalized phone + address + price. Keeping this separate from `id` means dedup logic can improve later without ever renaming or merging the post-level record.
apartment_id.title: Apartment Id

raw_excerpt.description: A short excerpt (1-2 sentences) around whatever text justified a signal -- never the full post or page. Keeping this short is a deliberate memory-budget decision, not an oversight. An over-length value is truncated (with a visible marker), not rejected -- see _truncate_raw_excerpt below for why.
raw_excerpt.title: Raw Excerpt

notes.description: Free-form human notes carried over from manual review.
notes.title: Notes

match_score.description: Percentage scale (0-100), not a 0-1 fraction -- a third external review correctly noted this had no bounds at all before, which meant the scale itself was undefined (a -40 or a 4000 both validated). 0-100 is chosen now and stated explicitly here because Phase 1's scoring engine is the first code that will actually populate this field, and it needs a documented convention to target rather than inventing one.
match_score.title: Match Score
